title: GL read-back multi-pair journal-entry batch (loan 10: disbursement pair plus fee pair) balances exactly
_note: Parity vector transcribing the loan-produced journal-entry batch read back from the journal-entries endpoint for loan entityId 10. This is the only committed observation with MORE THAN ONE PAIR: transaction L17 disburses (DEBIT OHLGR-Loan-Portfolio 100000.0, CREDIT OHLGR-Fund-Source 100000.0) and transaction L18 collects a fee (CREDIT OHLGR-Income-From-Fees 100.0, DEBIT OHLGR-Fund-Source 100.0). The batch therefore holds four legs over two distinct transaction ids, and sum(debits)=100100.0 == sum(credits)=100100.0. request.journal_entries transcribes each leg's transactionId, glAccountName, entryType.value and amount; amounts are raised to integer minor units (100000.0 -> 10000000, 100.0 -> 10000). expect.journal_entry_debits_minor and expect.journal_entry_credits_minor are the two independent side totals, each transcribed as the sum over EVERY leg, never a netting of the two OHLGR-Fund-Source legs and never a truncation after the first pair. The single-pair loan 12 capture (journalentries-loan-12-raw.json, transaction L20, 100000.0 each way) cannot grade this property: a one-pair batch balances under almost any defect. Nothing was computed by this promotion; the four legs and the two totals are transcriptions of the oracle's generated postings.

provenance.note: request.journal_entries and both expected totals are transcribed from the four pageItems of the committed capture journalentries-all-raw.json whose entityType.value is LOAN and entityId is 10 (transactionId L17 and L18). capture_case_id names L17, the disbursement transaction the batch opens with; the fee pair is L18 in the same capture. The capture is a filtered journal-entries page (totalFilteredRecords 18), so it is identified by the two transaction ids rather than an externalId.
